channel.title: AgentSlang blog
channel.description: Notes from building a language for models.

item.title: Clean Break v0.4: One C Host, Everything Else in ASL
item.description: The goal of v0.4: compiler, library and tooling in ASL with one small C host. What the tree holds today, and how far self-hosting has got.

item.title: A Small Host Boundary: What an ASL Program May Ask of Its Host
item.description: What the declared platform adapter lists, why the wasm32 target is the boundary actually enforced today (four host imports, everything else refused at compile time), and why deterministic replay is still a goal.

item.title: S-Expression Wire Frames vs. JSON-RPC: What the Notation Saves, and What Is Built
item.description: Why JSON's quotes, colons and commas cost tokens, one measured tool-call example (51 vs 18 cl100k_base tokens), and the ASN wire frames the agent bus implements today.

item.title: The Zero-Line-Number Invariant: Semantic Anchoring and AST Navigation in Autonomous Coding
item.description: Why line numbers make agent edits fragile, and how asl addresses code by symbol, anchor and exact text, failing loudly with ERR_NO_MATCH, ERR_AMBIGUOUS or ERR_STALE_BASE instead of editing the wrong span.

item.title: Small Models on Local Hardware: What AgentSlang Offers Them Today
item.description: Why delimiter-structured code suits small local models, the grammar token-masker and Ollama routing that exist today, and what is still unmeasured.

item.title: Why Small Local Models Struggle with Python, and Why S-Expressions Should Help
item.description: Why indentation-scoped Python is hard for small local models, how balanced S-expressions and a strict host check catch structural mistakes before anything runs, and the comparison we have not yet measured.

item.title: Beyond JSON-RPC: Why ASL Frames Agent Messages as S-Expressions
item.description: What JSON-RPC envelopes and escaped code strings cost a model on every tool call, one measured example (51 vs 15 tokens), the wire frame ASL implements today, and the AgP protocol that is still a design.

item.title: Killing Docker Spin-Up Latency: Why Agent Test Sandboxes Belong in Memory
item.description: Why agent test loops should move from containers to in-memory WebAssembly, what the ASL wasm32 compiler does today, and what a host test run costs now.

item.title: Why Autonomous LLMs Break on Human Languages (and What We Are Building Instead)
item.description: Why indentation and borrow-checked syntax trap LLMs in repair loops, and what balanced S-expressions with closed variants change.

item.title: Test Telemetry for Agents: Time, Memory and Assertion Counts in Every Receipt
item.description: What the strict ASL test runner reports today (assertion counts, GC allocation stats), how to measure time and memory around it, and the per-suite telemetry receipt we are building.

item.title: Beyond Flat Context: Tiered Memory and Tree Aggregation in AgentSlang
item.description: How AgentSlang keeps agent memory as plain ASN ledgers under .asl/mem today, and the recursive tiers, executable invariants, logical addresses and aggregation it is building toward.

item.title: Why Bash Wrappers Fail Coding Agents: Action Loops and Checks That Run Before Code Does
item.description: Why bash wrappers fail coding agents, how bounded reads, staged edits and the stage-0 host's pre-run checks help, and why a check that always passes is worse than none.

item.title: Why Disemvoweling Breaks BPE: How Naive Token Optimization Hurts Coding Agents
item.description: Measured token counts show that shortened identifiers like ctermtxt save nothing on o200k or cl100k, why synonym spellings cost repair turns, and the camelCase whole-word naming rule AgentSlang adopted.

item.title: Stop Making LLMs Do OS Work: Why Autonomous Coding Needs an ALU / Kernel Split
item.description: Why treating an LLM as scheduler, file system and interpreter at once makes agents fragile, which parts of a deterministic harness exist today (bounded reads, staged edits, host checks), and which are still being built.

item.title: The Single Grammar Doctrine: Why Multi-Agent Systems Need One Homoiconic Notation
item.description: Why agents juggling JSON, YAML, SVG and shell pay each format's escaping rules, and what one S-expression notation with tested renderers buys, measured on three examples.

item.title: Against Agent Framework Bloat: The Case for Radical Simplicity over Large Orchestrators
item.description: Why large orchestration frameworks fail a few turns into real work, and how the Ladder of Restraint, tools as forms and gate-closed steps keep agent systems small.

item.title: Why LLMs Choke on SVG XML: Vector Graphics as Native S-Expressions
item.description: Why raw SVG markup truncates under an output cap, and how ASN vector forms render to SVG with a single delimiter rule.

item.title: Git-Native Agent Memory: Versioned Ledgers and In-Process Vector Recall
item.description: Agent memory kept as Git-tracked ASN ledgers moves with branches and needs no hosted index; in-process vector recall over F64 arrays is being built on top.

item.title: Bound Literals, Unquoted Names: Rendering Relational S-Expressions to Postgres, SQLite, MySQL & ClickHouse
item.description: How asl-sql models queries as algebraic data so the dialect and every literal become parameters, and where that injection boundary still has gaps.

item.title: The Zero-Server IDE: Why We Are Building Agent Sandboxes That Run Inside a Browser Tab
item.description: The design for running compiler, tests, storage and agents inside a browser tab, and where it stands: this site already runs as ASL compiled to WebAssembly with four host imports, while the in-tab checker, OPFS repository and IDE are still to come.

item.title: Stop Your Agent from Faking Green Tests: Closure Checks and Anti-Hallucination Firewalls
item.description: The stage-0 host rejects invented names, wrong arity, unmarked effects, constant asserts and vacuous or false tests before anything runs; quote-grounded claims and workspace path jails cover the rest.

item.title: One Source Across Rust, TypeScript, Python & Wasm: The Case Against Multi-Language Glue Drift
item.description: Why re-implementing logic per language breeds drift, what ASL fixes in the language itself, what runs today (the reference host, LLVM to native and wasm32, asl-sql), and the source-level lowerings and differential gate still to come.

item.title: Debugging Autonomous Swarms Without Reading Their Logs
item.description: Observability for agent swarms as structured queries: import graphs and package cycle audits, token cost by file, workspace path jails and checked effect marking, with per-run capability grants still to come.

item.title: Building a Developer Cockpit for Synthetic Intelligences
item.description: How the asl toolbelt serves coding agents: symbol-sized reads, S-expression receipts, host checks for names and arity, staged edits and workspace path jails, and what is still missing.

item.title: Inter-Agent Protocol (AgP): Replacing Natural Language Chatter with Typed S-Expression Frames
item.description: AgP specifies sigil-headed S-expression frames, a closed ten-keyword error taxonomy and context-isolated handoffs for agent-to-agent messages; the spec and skill exist, and the enforcing decoder is not built yet.

item.title: Stop Burning Money on JSON Context: Structural Compaction Saves Tokens, Abbreviation Does Not
item.description: Measured under BPE tokenizers: keyword abbreviations tie or lose, naming conventions move a corpus by under 2%, and positional frames and tables cut 40.0% to 64.7% against spaced keyed JSON on three samples (13.6% to 40% against minified JSON).

item.title: Prefix Heads and Closed Variants: Why S-Expressions and Algebraic Types Suit LLMs
item.description: Why prefix heads, balanced delimiters and exhaustively matched enums suit autoregressive generation, and which of these the host checks today.

item.title: The Context Tax: How AST Interface Extraction Stops Agent Working Memory Rot
item.description: How exported-interface stubs cut what a subagent must read, measured on one module and with the repository-wide benchmark still to run.
